+name: Security
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: [main]
+  pull_request:
+    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
+  schedule:
+    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+# Least-privilege default; jobs escalate individually when needed.
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+# Provide Git config to actions/checkout itself; checkout runs git init before
+# any workflow step can configure Git.
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  codeql:
+    name: CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-codeql-${{ matrix.language }}
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    permissions:
+      actions: read
+      contents: read
+      security-events: write
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        language: [javascript-typescript, actions]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+
+      - name: Initialize CodeQL
+        uses: github/codeql-action/init@v4
+        with:
+          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
+
+      - name: Autobuild
+        uses: github/codeql-action/autobuild@v4
+
+      - name: Analyze
+        uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@v4
+
+  dependency-review:
+    name: Dependency Review
+    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-dependency-review
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      pull-requests: write
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+
+      - name: Review dependency changes
+        uses: actions/dependency-review-action@v5
+        with:
+          fail-on-severity: high
+          comment-summary-in-pr: on-failure

+# Issue 2150 / PR 2151 investigation
+
+Collected and analyzed on 2026-08-11 UTC. This document is the index and
+conclusion for the raw evidence stored beside it. All timestamps below are UTC.
+
+## Scope and method
+
+The investigation covered:
+
+1. every issue and pull-request body, event, commit, review, conversation
+   comment, and inline review comment available at collection time;
+2. the complete logs and job metadata for the cited failing default-branch run
+   and the prepared PR's initial run;
+3. a fresh clone and full file tree of the JavaScript CI/CD template at commit
+   `9af528` (release `0.11.27`), including its open and closed issue history;

+## Root-cause and solution matrix
+
+### 1. Node 24 command-loader failure (three failed jobs)
+
+**Observed:** The default suite failed at `src/log-upload.lib.mjs`; log-file
+verification and all memory checks failed at `src/memory-check.mjs`. Each
+ultimately reported `TypeError: $ is not a function`. See the full log around
+lines 17,810, 18,953, and 19,292, plus the extracted diagnostics.
+
+**Root cause:** Hive Mind intentionally uses `use-m` for runtime dependencies.
+Bare package names allowed `use-m@8.15.0` to resolve npm's mutable `latest` tag.
+`command-stream@0.19.0` was published 141 minutes before the failing main run
+and its package metadata selects `./src/$.cjs` as `main`. Node 23+ adds a
+synthetic `module.exports` named export to CommonJS namespace objects. `use-m`
+does not classify that property as namespace metadata, so on Node 24 it returns
+the namespace object instead of unwrapping the callable default export. Thus
+destructuring `$` produces `undefined`. Node 20 exposes only `default`, which
+`use-m` unwraps, explaining the control result.
+
+The version/export matrix in `command-stream-export-matrix.txt` and
+`use-m-command-stream-version-matrix.txt` isolates all variables. The reusable
+experiment is `experiments/issue-2150/inspect-command-stream-exports.mjs`.
+
+**Implemented solution:**
+
+- pin `use-m` bootstrap URLs to `use-m@8.15.0` on both CDNs;
+- centrally pin all eight runtime-loaded npm dependencies, including
+  `command-stream@0.18.0`, rather than repairing one caller;
+- normalize only the distinctive Node namespace shape where `default` and
+  `module.exports` exist and are identical, preserving genuine ESM namespaces;
+- make the CI preinstaller consume the same central version map;
+- validate that the loaded `$` export is callable at a common early boundary;
+- retain opt-in pin and normalization tracing under `HIVE_MIND_USE_M_DEBUG`.
+
+**Alternatives considered:** Pinning only `command-stream` removes today's
+failure but leaves seven packages mutable. Downgrading CI to Node 20 violates
+the package engine and hides the interoperability defect. Replacing `use-m`
+throughout is much larger and unnecessary for this PR. The upstream fix should
+teach `use-m` to recognize Node's `module.exports` marker; issue #72 proposes
+that change.
+
+The pinned aliases also exposed a second upstream defect during clean global
+installation: npm refuses to install `zx-v-8.8.5` when the existing
+`zx-v-latest` alias owns the shared `bin/zx` symlink. `use-m` does not disable
+bin links or recover from this expected alias collision, so pinning alone could
+make a previously initialized machine fail with `EEXIST`. The loader now
+repairs only this narrowly verified case: it confirms the conflicting symlink
+belongs to another alias of the same package, then installs the pinned alias
+with npm's `--no-bin-links`. It refuses unrelated conflicts. The isolated
+before/after reproducer and tests are preserved, and issue #73 proposes the
+equivalent upstream fix.
+
+### 2. Memory-check false-positive help assertion
+
+**Observed:** The `--help` subtest printed the full stack trace above and still
+reported `PASSED`, while seven functional subtests failed.
+
+**Root cause:** The assertion accepted generic output/nonzero behavior instead
+of requiring successful help output. Any startup crash therefore satisfied it.
+
+**Implemented solution:** Require exit code zero plus expected help semantics.
+`test-memory-check-after.log` and the end-to-end reproduction show 10/10 tests
+passing; the before evidence preserves the false positive.
+
+### 3. Command and dry-run false negatives
+
+**Observed:** Multiple smoke paths used `|| true` or converted a command error
+to a warning. A crash could therefore leave the job green. The release dry-run
+also treated timeout status and every unrelated failure identically.
+
+**Root cause:** Status suppression was added for expected timeouts and optional
+cleanup, but its scope covered startup/import/argument errors too. Piped output
+also hid the program status unless `PIPESTATUS` was inspected. After removing
+the suppression, the log smoke test exposed a second defect: it targeted the
+nonexistent `test/repo`, so a correct command deterministically returned 1.
+
+**Implemented solution:** Help/version smoke checks now fail on command errors;
+the log test uses a non-GitHub URL, requires status 1 plus the exact validation
+reason, rejects timeout/runtime-error output, and then verifies the generated
+log. This removes live-repository dependence without accepting arbitrary
+failures. Other dry-run paths no longer swallow status. Cleanup-only
+best-effort operations remain explicitly non-fatal.
+
+### 4. Cancelled/failed jobs could yield a misleading pipeline result
+
+**Observed:** The workflow had no terminal observer. GitHub represents a job
+killed by `timeout-minutes` as `cancelled`, and dependent write jobs simply skip.
+This can make a required timeout indistinguishable from a superseded PR run.
+
+**Root cause:** Individual `if: !cancelled()` gates safely stop writers but do
+not convert a main-branch cancellation into a workflow failure.
+
+**Implemented solution:** The template's `check-pipeline-status.sh` pattern was
+adapted as a final job that observes every other release job. Any failure is an
+error. Cancellation on `main` is an error; cancellation on a PR is a warning so
+superseded read-only runs remain cancellable. A structural regression test
+ensures newly added jobs cannot silently escape the observer.
+
+### 5. Git and JavaScript-action runtime warnings
+
+**Observed:** Every checkout emitted Git's default-initial-branch hint and
+setup-node v5 emitted `DEP0040` (`punycode`) warnings under the forced Node 24
+action runtime.
+
+**Root cause:** Git initializes checkout's temporary repository before a normal
+workflow step can configure it. Older action bundles brought older runtime
+dependencies.
+
+**Implemented solution:** Supply `init.defaultBranch=main` through Git's
+`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY/VALUE` environment contract, available to checkout from
+process start. Upgrade every checkout and setup-node occurrence in both
+existing workflows to v6. Security uses the same versions. Regression tests
+scan every workflow, not one occurrence.
+
+### 6. Nineteen file-headroom warnings
+
+**Observed:** Nineteen `.mjs` files and `release.yml` exceeded the repository's
+1,350-line warning threshold, several at exactly 1,500. They did not fail the
+hard 1,500-line gate but created real concurrent-merge risk.
+
+**Root cause:** Responsibilities and whitespace accumulated while the hard
+ceiling allowed files to reach the point where normal parallel PRs could push
+them over the limit.
+
+**Implemented solution:** Extracted Claude connection validation, pure GitHub
+URL parsing, and the dynamic tool-specific uncommitted-change loader into three
+tested modules. In the remaining files only blank lines were removed or
+consecutive line comments were joined without deleting comment text. The
+mechanical accounting is in `line-headroom-compaction-report.txt`. Every warned
+file is now at or below the 1,350-line early-warning threshold, and extracted
+modules leave their former parents smaller still. An AST/template-literal audit
+also verifies that the mechanical compaction preserved runtime values and code
+structure. The final line-limit log has no warning annotation. The 1,500 hard
+limit and 1,350 early-warning policy were not weakened.
+
+### 7. Dependency vulnerabilities and install-script warning
+
+**Observed:** `npm audit` found four high-severity transitive vulnerabilities:
+`brace-expansion`, `fast-uri`, `flatted`, and `js-yaml`. A clean npm 11 install
+also warned that `@sentry/node-cpu-profiler@2.4.2` had an unreviewed install
+script.
+
+**Root cause:** The lockfile resolved vulnerable transitive versions and npm's
+new lifecycle-script review policy had no project decision for the profiler.
+
+**Implemented solution:** `npm audit fix` refreshed only compatible transitive
+resolutions, taking the audit from four high findings to zero. The existing
+Sentry profiler's build check was reviewed and approved through npm's official
+command, producing an exact-version `allowScripts` entry rather than trusting
+all future releases. A clean Node 24 `npm ci` installs 443 packages with no
+warning and audits 444 packages with zero vulnerabilities.
+
+### 8. Missing continuous security analysis
+
+**Observed:** Hive Mind had secret scanning in local/pre-commit dependencies and
+an npm audit step, but no CodeQL workflow or PR dependency-review enforcement.
+The JavaScript template has both.
+
+**Root cause:** The repository's older specialized workflow predated the
+template security workflow and had not inherited it.
+
+**Implemented solution:** Added the template-aligned `security.yml`: CodeQL for
+both JavaScript/TypeScript and Actions on PRs, main, manual dispatch, and weekly
+schedule; dependency review on PRs fails at high severity; permissions are
+least-privilege, jobs are bounded by timeouts, and read-only runs cancel when
+superseded.
+
+### 9. Duplication output and initial green PR run (not defects)
+
+`jscpd` reports clone locations as diagnostic output. Hive Mind already limits
+analysis to JavaScript and fails above 11%; the final measured duplication is
+9.5%, so suppressing clone locations would hide useful evidence. Template
+issue #126 concerned a different configuration (`format: console`) that
+analyzed zero files; Hive Mind does not have that false positive.
+
+The initial PR run's green status is also not evidence of a corrected pipeline:
+change detection deliberately excludes `.gitkeep`, as required by the best
+practices document. The job graph correctly skipped substantive work. Fresh
+post-push runs must be matched to the final commit SHA before acceptance.
+

+## Online and reusable-component research
+
+Only primary/maintainer sources informed implementation:
+
+- [Node.js ESM/CommonJS interoperability](https://nodejs.org/download/release/v24.19.0/docs/api/esm.html#commonjs-namespaces)
+  documents the `default` and `'module.exports'` CommonJS namespace markers
+  that explain the Node 24-only shape.
+- [`actions/setup-node`](https://github.com/actions/setup-node) documents that
+  v6 uses the Node 24 action runtime, recommends explicitly selecting Node, and
+  shows checkout/setup-node v6 together.
+- [GitHub dependency-review configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/manage-your-dependency-security/configure-dependency-review-action)
+  recommends a PR action with explicit `contents: read` and severity policy.
+- [GitHub CodeQL for Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-scanning/codeql/codeql-queries/actions-built-in-queries)
+  confirms that workflow permissions and other Actions-specific weaknesses are
+  analyzable, motivating the `actions` matrix entry.
+- [npm `approve-scripts`](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-approve-scripts/)
+  states that this command is the recommended way to manage `allowScripts` and
+  defaults to exact-version approvals.
+- The requested [JavaScript pipeline template](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)
+  supplied the security workflow and terminal-gate patterns. Its existing
+  issues [#41](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/41),
+  [#99](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/99),
+  [#123](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/123),
+  and [#126](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/126)
+  prevent duplicate reports.
+- Upstream [`use-m` issue #72](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/72)
+  records the Node 24 CommonJS namespace defect, while
+  [`use-m` issue #73](https://github.com/link-foundation/use-m/issues/73)
+  records the npm alias-bin collision discovered while validating the pinning
+  strategy.

+No additional library is needed. Node's namespace is safely normalized at the
+existing loader boundary; adopting another process library would not repair
+`use-m`'s module classification. CodeQL, dependency-review-action, npm audit,

+[
+  {
+    "body": "## Summary

Implements `/task --ci-cd <repository>` as the issue-creation-only fallback for `/fix --ci-cd` (issue #2121).

The command now:

1. accepts both ASCII `--ci-cd` and the reported typographic `—ci-cd` spelling;
2. collects the target repository's languages, default-branch commit, and CI/CD runs;
3. creates the same typed CI/CD remediation issue as `/fix --ci-cd`;
4. returns the full created-issue URL without starting `/fix` or `/solve`; and
5. tells the user to reply with `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge` to continue normally.

## Root cause

Telegram's shared argument parser already normalized the reported em dash and tokenized the option before the repository URL. The `/task` handler, however, only distinguished ordinary issue creation from split mode. It therefore sent the complete option-and-URL line to the free-form issue parser, which could not find the repository in its expected standalone form and returned “Missing GitHub repository URL.”

The network-backed CI/CD collector also lived inside executable `fix.mjs`, preventing `/task` from reusing only the issue-creation stage without duplication or spawning the full workflow.

## Implementation

- Extract `prepareCiCdIssue()` and `createCiCdIssue()` into a shared service used by both `/fix` and `/task`.
- Add a dedicated `/task --ci-cd` handler path before ordinary issue parsing.
- Preserve the existing title/body builders, commit-to-branch run fallback, Bug type, and `bug` label fallback.
- Reject missing repositories and issue/PR URLs; reject combining `--ci-cd` with split mode.
- Document the fallback in all four maintained README/help locales.
- Add a minor changeset.
- Add the requested deep case study and machine-readable evidence/source catalogs under `docs/case-studies/issue-2121/`.

## Reproduction and regression coverage

Before this change:

```text
/task —ci-cd https://github.com/link-assistant/agent
→ Missing GitHub repository URL
```

The regression test now sends that exact command shape through `handleTaskCommand()` and asserts:

- the parsed repository reaches the shared CI/CD issue generator;
- no managed task or `/fix` execution starts;
- the created issue URL is returned; and
- the exact continuation solve flags are shown.

Additional tests cover ASCII parsing, invalid repository inputs, shared GitHub context collection, prompt generation, and typed issue creation.

## Verification

- `npm test` — all 358 default test files passed
- `npm run format:check`
- `npm run lint`
- `npm run check:duplication`
- `node tests/docs-validation.mjs`
- `node tests/test-docs-language-sync.mjs`
- `node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`
- `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`
- focused task and CI/CD suites: 28/28 each

Closes #2121.
",
+    "mergedAt": "2026-07-31T13:42:15Z",
+    "number": 2122,
+    "title": "/task --ci-cd: create CI/CD remediation issues without /fix (#2121)",
+    "url": "https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2122"
+  },
+  {
+    "body": "## Problem

`/task --ci-cd https://github.com/link-assistant/agent` created
[link-assistant/agent#287](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/issues/287), whose
"Recent CI/CD runs on `main`" table has **20 rows for only 2 workflows** — the same
*JS CI/CD Pipeline* (14 rows) and *Rust CI/CD Pipeline* (6 rows) repeated for commits
spanning 2026-04-25 … 2026-07-30 — and a summary of "CI/CD runs found: 20 (9 not passing)"
that counts months-old failures as current.

## Root cause

`/fix --ci-cd` and `/task --ci-cd` share `prepareCiCdIssue()`. It lists the runs of the
latest default-branch commit; when that commit produced none — verified for `agent`'s
`fd42c4b` ("0.25.4"): `actions/runs?head_sha=fd42c4b…` returns `total_count: 0` — it falls
back to `actions/runs?branch=main`, which returns runs **across many commits**.
`buildRunsSection()` mapped that array 1:1 to table rows, and `summarizeRunFailures()`
counted it raw. `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs` has no "latest run per workflow"
option, so the collapse has to happen client-side — and nothing did it.

## Fix

- `runWorkflowKey()` — workflow identity: `workflow_id`, then `path`, then `name`; a run
  with no identifying field is never treated as a duplicate.
- `dedupeRunsByWorkflow()` — keeps the most recent run per workflow (`created_at`, then
  `run_attempt`, then `id`), preserving input order. `countDuplicateRuns()` reports how
  many rows it drops.
- `buildRunsSection()` deduplicates and gained `includeCommit`, so the branch-fallback
  table shows which commit each surviving run belongs to.
- `summarizeRunFailures()` / `buildCiCdIssueBody()` count the deduplicated set, so the
  table and the "CI/CD runs found" line always agree.
- The runs query now selects `workflow_id`, `path`, `created_at`, `run_attempt`, and the
  fallback fetches `per_page=100` instead of `20` — after collapsing, a workflow whose last
  run is older than the 20 most recent would otherwise disappear entirely.
- `prepareCiCdIssue()` returns `fetchedRuns`/`duplicateRuns` and logs
  `ℹ️ Collapsed N older CI/CD run(s) …`, which `/fix` prints.

## Reproduction and verification

Regenerating the issue body from the *exact* 20 runs behind agent#287
(`docs/case-studies/issue-2125/data/`) now yields:

```
| Workflow | Status | Conclusion | Commit | Run |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JS CI/CD Pipeline | completed | failure | `cff4148` | [run](.../30572373896) |
| Rust CI/CD Pipeline | completed | failure | `7af549d` | [run](.../28688932169) |
```

with `CI/CD runs found: 2 (2 not passing)`. Full "before" payload, the regenerated body and
the analysis are in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2125`](docs/case-studies/issue-2125/README.md).

## Tests

`tests/test-fix-ci-cd.mjs` (suite `default`) gains four regression tests, including an
end-to-end `prepareCiCdIssue()` run through a stubbed `gh` that reproduces the release-commit
→ branch-fallback → duplicate-row path and asserts the stale run is gone, the count is not
inflated, and the verbose collapse line is emitted.

Fixes #2125
",
+    "mergedAt": "2026-07-31T18:57:22Z",
+    "number": 2126,
+    "title": "fix(2125): collapse duplicate CI/CD runs in generated issues",
+    "url": "https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2126"
+  },
+  {
+    "body": "## Summary

Implements `/fix --ci-cd <repository>` (issue #1733): a command that **automatically generates and solves a CI/CD remediation issue** for a target repository, from the CLI or from Telegram.

Given a repository, `/fix --ci-cd`:

1. **Detects languages** via the GitHub `/languages` API and selects the matching CI/CD templates, **ordered by detected language** (byte-weighted; JavaScript + TypeScript merge into one template).
2. **Inspects the latest default-branch commit** and lists its CI/CD runs in the issue. Release/tag commits frequently have no runs of their own, so it **falls back to the most recent default-branch runs** (clearly relabelled "Recent CI/CD runs on `<branch>`").
3. **Creates the remediation issue**, reusing the title and description of [web-capture#139](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/139) **exactly, minus the parts `--development-log` and `--deep-analysis` already provide**, and linking to `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`.
4. **Hands the issue off to `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge`**, forwarding every option `/fix` does not consume itself (e.g. `--tool`, `--model`, `--think`).

The upstream case-study paragraph is **retired and never represented in the generated prompt**. `--development-log` is its sole replacement and collects under `./dev/log/issues/{id}/pulls/{pr}`; no option combination, including `--no-solve` or a partial option set, restores the old folder convention. | Paragraph | `providedBy` | Dropped when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Compile data / retired case study | — | always excluded; replaced by `--development-log` |
| Provide debug output | `--deep-analysis` | `--deep-analysis` is passed |
| Report upstream template issues | `--deep-analysis` | `--deep-analysis` is passed |
| Compare full file tree / best-practices link / keep-working | — | never |

- **There is no legacy fallback.** Review feedback clarified that the upstream case-study paragraph conflicts with `--development-log`; it was removed as a constant and paragraph entry, rather than merely hidden by the default option set. Hive Mind commands kept dying at startup while loading `command-stream`, in two
alternating shapes. From the two logs attached to the issue — the *same* command,
`fix https://github.com/link-assistant/agent --ci-cd --attach-logs --verbose`, one
image apart:

```text
# 2.11.1
npm error ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '.../command-stream-v-latest/examples'
Failed to install command-stream@latest globally into '...' after 3 attempts.
```

```text
# 2.10.2
Failed to import module from '.../command-stream-v-latest/src/$.mjs?use-m-retry=1'.
Caused by: Cannot find module '.../command-stream-v-latest/src/shell-parser.mjs'
```

The missing file changed every run (`shell-parser.mjs`, `terminal-capture.mjs`,
`$.trace.mjs`), and `npm pack command-stream@0.17.2 --dry-run --json` shows all of
them are published — so this was never a bad release.

## Root cause

`use()` runs one `npm install -g <alias>@npm:<package>@<version>` per call and has
**no in-flight deduplication**. Node evaluates sibling top-level-await subgraphs
concurrently ([proved locally](experiments/issue-2113/prove-top-level-await-concurrency.mjs):
peak concurrency 3 of 3), and 38 modules under `src/` load `command-stream` through
`use()`, 31 of them at top level — so a cold container running `fix` launches **six
simultaneous global installs of one directory**. npm does not lock the global prefix,
so those installs delete and re-extract each other's trees: the loser gets `ENOTEMPTY`,
and whoever reads a half-extracted tree gets `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for whichever file
was not written yet.

use-m's own recovery amplifies it: `installPackage()` runs
`removePackageAlias(packagePath, 'incomplete')` after *every* failed attempt, so the
loser recursively deletes the tree the winner just installed successfully — which is
exactly how a process that saw no error at all ends up with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

**Retrying cannot help, because every retry re-enters the same race** — visible verbatim
in the 2.11.1 log, where all three of use-m's attempts fail on the same path within nine
seconds.

Reproduced three ways, all recorded under
[`docs/case-studies/issue-2113/raw/`](docs/case-studies/issue-2113/raw):

| Reproduction | Result |
| --- | --- |
| npm alone, 24 concurrent installs of one alias | 22/24 fail, alias gone afterwards |
| npm alone, 5 concurrent installs of *different* packages (control) | 0/5 fail |
| stock use-m 8.14.4 from the CDN, 8 concurrent `use('command-stream')` | 2/8 fail |
| end to end, 24 concurrent loads, unguarded | **24/24 fail in 54.8 s** |
| end to end, 24 concurrent loads, guarded | **0/24 in 3.3 s** |

The control is what narrows the fix to a **per-alias** lock rather than a global install
lock that would needlessly serialise unrelated dependencies.

### Why the "two commands" workaround appeared to work

The issue reports that splitting the work into `/task --ci-cd` + `/claude <issue>` never
fails. That is consistent with the race, not against it:
[`measure-entrypoint-fanout.mjs`](experiments/issue-2113/measure-entrypoint-fanout.mjs)
walks each binary's import graph and counts reachable modules that top-level-await a
`command-stream` load:

```text
binary              modules   cold burst (static)   reachable (incl. dynamic)
task                93        6                     8
fix                 95        6                     8
review              90        5                     9
solve               156       1                     25
```

`/task --ci-cd` never spawns anything — `src/telegram-task-command.lib.mjs:177` calls
`createCiCdIssueFn()` in the already-warm bot process, so it installs nothing — and
`/claude <issue>` spawns `solve`, whose cold burst is exactly one loader. The workaround
reduced exposure; it did not remove it.

`src/use-m-single-flight.lib.mjs` (new, Node built-ins only) wraps `use()` inside
`ensureUseM()`, so all 72 files that bootstrap through it inherit three guards with no
call-site changes:

1. **Per-specifier single flight** — a `Map` from specifier to the in-flight promise,
   evicted on rejection so failures stay retryable. Collapses the whole cold wave into
   one install.
2. **In-process per-alias mutex** — a promise chain keyed by the *alias*

   `use('command-stream/foo')` serialise while unrelated packages still install in
   parallel.
3. **Cross-process advisory lock** — atomic `mkdir` on `<alias>.lock`, `utimes`
   heartbeat, stale-steal and timeout, so a bot, a container and a CI step sharing one
   npm prefix cannot collide either. Degrades to in-process-only if the lock root is
   unusable; relocatable with `HIVE_MIND_USE_M_LOCK_DIR`. Built-ins (`use('fs')`) are
   deduplicated but never take the lock.

`useWithRetry()` is kept underneath as recovery for corruption that already exists — the
new layer is prevention, which retries could not provide.

The guard deliberately has no dependencies: it is the thing that makes loading
dependencies safe, so it cannot itself require `proper-lockfile` or `p-memoize`. Their
designs are followed (`mkdir` strategy, `mtime` staleness; `stale: 10000`/`update: stale/2`
informed `DEFAULT_STALE_MS = 15000`/`DEFAULT_HEARTBEAT_MS = 1000`), documented in
[`research.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-2113/research.md).

Both attached logs were produced **with `--verbose`** and contained no loader output at

```text

[use-m] use('command-stream') joined an in-flight load (alias command-stream-v-latest)
[use-m] use('command-stream') loaded in 2841ms
```

1. **Timeout-cancelled CI was misclassified as "requires review".** A job that hits its `timeout-minutes` limit surfaces as a **check-run** with conclusion `cancelled`, but the **parent workflow run** concludes `failure`. `getDetailedCIStatus` inspects check-runs only, so the auto-merge loop saw the lone `cancelled` check, posted a **"Cancelled CI/CD Requires Review"** comment, and stopped — even though the workflow run had failed and *other jobs in it had also failed*.
2. **The session finished with no log attached despite `--attach-logs`.** Every log-attachment path in `solve.mjs` is conditional, and the stop-for-human-review exits can `return` before any iteration uploads a log.

## Root cause

GitHub reports a timed-out job at two levels with different conclusions:

| Inspect… | Timeout looks like… | Manual cancel looks like… |
| --- | --- | --- |
| check-runs only (old behaviour) | `cancelled` ❌ | `cancelled` |
| workflow runs (the fix) | `failure` ✅ | `cancelled` |

The real teleton run `27821270533` concluded `failure` with jobs `Build (Runtime) (22)`, `Deploy artifacts`, `OpenAPI` all **failed** plus `Build (Runtime) (20)` **cancelled** (timeout) — yet the tool stopped for review. Full evidence and analysis: [`docs/case-studies/issue-1952/`](./docs/case-studies/issue-1952/README.md).

## Changes

### R1 + R2 — classify cancelled CI by workflow-run conclusions
- New pure helper `classifyCancelledCIByWorkflowRuns` + `FAILURE_LIKE_WORKFLOW_RUN_CONCLUSIONS` (`failure`, `timed_out`, `startup_failure`) in `src/cancelled-ci-rerun.lib.mjs`.
- `getMergeBlockers` (`src/solve.auto-merge-helpers.lib.mjs`) cancelled branch now fetches the workflow runs for the SHA and classifies:
  - **pending** (any run not yet terminal) → `ci_pending` → keep waiting until *all* checks are terminal (R2).
  - **failure** (any completed failure-like run) → `ci_failure` → restart the AI to fix it (R1; R2 coexisting failures).
  - **cancelled** → original re-triggerable flow (genuine manual cancellation).
- `src/solve.auto-merge.lib.mjs`: the "Cancelled CI/CD Requires Review" stop path is skipped when a `ci_failure` blocker coexists.
- `src/github-merge-ci.lib.mjs`: `startup_failure` now counts as a failing run (applied codebase-wide, R7).

### R3 — guarantee a log is always attached
- `attachLogToGitHub` (`src/github.lib.mjs`) sets `global.logAttachedToGitHub = true` on **every** successful upload (both upload branches).
- New `attachFinalLogIfMissing` (`src/attach-logs-guarantee.lib.mjs`) runs as the last step of `solve.mjs`: attaches the cumulative session log when `--attach-logs` is on, a PR exists, and nothing attached yet, then reconciles `logsAttached` so `endWorkSession` does not double-post.

### R4/R5/R6
- `docs/case-studies/issue-1952/` — downloaded evidence + deep analysis (timeline, requirements R1–R8, root causes, existing-component review). Verbose logging added in the cancelled branch (off by default). No third-party repo bug to report — the behaviour was entirely in hive-mind's own logic; GitHub Actions behaves as documented.

## How to reproduce (before the fix)
A PR whose CI workflow run concludes `failure` while one of its jobs is `cancelled` by `timeout-minutes`: the old code posted "Cancelled CI/CD Requires Review" and stopped instead of restarting the AI, and finished the session with no attached log.

## Tests
- `tests/test-cancelled-timeout-fail-1952.mjs` — 13 tests. Reproduces the teleton case (workflow-run `failure` + cancelled check → `failure`) and covers `timed_out`/`startup_failure`/manual-cancel/`stale`/mixed/in-progress/queued/empty + wiring.
- `tests/test-attach-logs-safety-net-1952.mjs` — 9 tests. Global flag set only on real uploads; `attachFinalLogIfMissing` disabled / no-PR / already-attached / fires-as-last-resort; solve.mjs wiring.

Both pass locally; the changeset bumps `@link-assistant/hive-mind` (patch).

| --- | --- | --- |

scripts/test-auto-fork-option.sh reported none of its three assertions:
each failed branch printed "Could not verify ..." and the script carried
on to exit 0.

This was not a latent risk. The marker the dry-run checks grep for first
appears ~32s into the run, because solve.mjs makes several GitHub API
calls before reaching the auto-fork decision — and the script killed the
command with `timeout 10s`. Both greps had been failing on every run
while the job stayed green. Reproduced locally: restoring the 10s
timeout now fails the script with exactly those two checks red.

- test-auto-fork-option.sh: realistic timeouts, every check asserts, and
  a hermetic --help check that does not depend on the network.
- check-file-line-limits.sh: a missing release.yml was a warning that
  skipped the check entirely; it is now an error.
- scripts/shell-lint.lib.mjs + tests: flag any `else` branch that reports
  a failure without failing. Branches that record the failure for a later
  check are exempt; deliberately non-fatal ones must say so with an
  explicit `# shell-lint: allow-nonfatal` marker and a reason.

ShellCheck does not cover this — an `else` that only echoes is valid
bash, so judging it needs repo-specific intent.",

+      "messageBody": "F14 — the concurrency policy was inverted:

    cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}

It cancelled in-progress runs on main — the one branch that publishes —
and queued them everywhere else. A release cancelled between `npm
publish` and the `git push` of the version bump leaves the registry
ahead of the repository: the same split-brain state as F4 and F5,
reached by a different route. Now main queues and PR branches cancel,
which is also where the wasted runners were.

F13 — nine jobs guarded their `if:` with `always()`, which is true even
after a cancellation, so they defeated the policy above. release.yml
documents this rule at the top of the file (from the #1274 and #1278
case studies) but applied it only to the Docker jobs. Five used bare
`always()`; four paired it with a contradictory `!cancelled()`.

Verified semantics with a real YAML parse: exactly 9 of 25 jobs changed,
each only in the leading term, the other 16 byte-identical. Note that
`if: !cancelled() && ...` must be wrapped in ${{ }} — a leading `!` is a
YAML tag, and the previous always() spelling did not need this.

Also extracts two Docker blocks from release.yml into scripts/. The
timeout-minutes added in 0e4eb599 had pushed the file to 1512 lines,
over the 1500-line limit — which no CI run caught, because the missing
changeset failed the changeset gate and every other job was skipped.
That changeset is added here too.",

getClaudeEnv() builds the child environment by spreading process.env. For
adaptive-thinking-only models it explicitly deletes an inherited
MAX_THINKING_TOKENS, but nothing did the same for CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL.
The block below it only ever assigns, so on every path that computes no
level the parent's value survived into the child:

  - a model supporting no effort levels at all (haiku), which skips the
    enclosing supportsEffortLevel() branch entirely;
  - --think off on a non-adaptive model, where neither inner branch fires.

Claude Code exports this variable and hive-mind's agents run under Claude
Code, so the leak fired in the ordinary case: 'haiku --think high'
inherited effort=max for a model the codebase classifies as supporting
none. Fixed by mirroring the existing MAX_THINKING_TOKENS sanitisation.

This also made the suite return opposite verdicts for the same commit.
CI runs without the variable and stayed green; run the same tests inside
Claude Code and test-opus-47-model-support.mjs failed with 5 errors. It
now passes 166/0 under a polluted environment as well as a clean one.

Adds effort-level-env-leak-2082.test.mjs, which pins the leak, the
behaviour that had to survive the fix (issue #2032's lowest-effort
mapping for adaptive-only models on --think off), and the general
invariant that the result is independent of the ambient shell.

Three sibling variables leak identically and are confirmed present in the
agent environment (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT, CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW,
CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE). Deliberately left alone: no sanitisation
precedent, no failing test, and plausibly intentional user config. Recorded
in the dev log for an explicit decision rather than a silent change.

Also documents F21 (the tests/ lint gap), F22 (this leak) and F23 (a
pre-existing flake in test-issue-1209-overrides.mjs, root-caused to a
live unpkg.com fetch on every bot startup against a fixed 12s kill).",

+      "messageBody": "Commit fd3a44ef silenced timers/no-leaked-timers on this helper with
exitTimer.unref?.(). unref does not just make a timer cancellable - it
removes it from the handles keeping the event loop alive. That callback
is what settles the awaited closeScreenSession, so Node exited with the
await still pending: exit 13 on CI (run 29690457864, Node 24), and a
silent pass locally on Node 20, where unsettled top-level await is not
detected at all.

Capture the timer and clear it from inside its own callback instead. It
stays referenced until it fires, cb(0) settles the await, and the handle
is released - satisfying both the lint rule and the runtime.

Audited the other six files whose timers that lint pass touched: unref
was added in exactly one place, and every added clearTimeout runs after
the awaited work, so it can only no-op on an already-fired timer.

The suite was re-run under Node 24 rather than the sandbox's Node 20,
since the project's own engines field requires >=24 and the older
runtime cannot observe this failure mode.",

+  "body": "## Summary

A job killed by its own `timeout-minutes` is reported by GitHub Actions as **`cancelled`**, not **`failure`**. A workflow run whose only non-success job is cancelled inherits the run conclusion `cancelled` too — which on the runs list is visually indistinguishable from "a human pressed cancel" or "a newer push superseded this run". It is grey, not red. It does not appear in the failed-runs filter and it sends no failure notification.

`release.yml` in this template has no job that observes the aggregate result, so a timing-out job produces a silently-green-looking pipeline.

This is not hypothetical. In [link-assistant/formal-ai](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai), which is derived from this template, **18 consecutive `CI/CD Pipeline` runs on `main` concluded `cancelled` over three days** while `Auto Release` was timing out. Nobody triaged them, because nothing looked broken. The damage: **11 versions (0.326.2 … 0.333.0) were published to crates.io and tagged in git with no GitHub Release at all**, because `Create GitHub Release` sits after the Docker publish step and was never reached.

## Reproducible example

```yaml
name: repro
on: workflow_dispatch
jobs:
  slow:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 1
    steps:
      - run: sleep 300   # killed at 1m
  other:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - run: echo ok
```

Dispatch it. The `slow` job is killed and annotated *"The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 1m0s"* — and both the job and the **whole run** conclude `cancelled`. `gh run list` shows no failure. Add `if: failure()` to any step and observe that it does not fire.

## Workaround

Set every job's `timeout-minutes` well above the tool's own internal timeout (e.g. Playwright's `globalTimeout`, `pytest-timeout`, `cargo nextest --slow-timeout`) so the *tool* aborts first, exits non-zero, and the job reports `failure`. This only helps for jobs that have such a tool.

## Suggested fix

Add a terminal gate job that `needs:` every other job and runs `if: always()`. The key nuance — and the reason an off-the-shelf action like [`re-actors/alls-green`](https://github.com/re-actors/alls-green) is not quite right here — is that a cancellation must be treated **differently on the default branch**. `release.yml` already sets

```yaml
concurrency:
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
```

so `main` is never superseded, and a cancelled job there can **only** be a timeout or a deliberate manual cancel. On other refs, a cancellation is the ordinary superseded-run case and must stay a warning, or every force-push would go red.

```yaml
  pipeline-status:
    name: Pipeline Status
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    if: always()
    needs: [ ...every other job... ]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Fail the run when a required job was cancelled or failed
        env:
          NEEDS_JSON: ${{ toJSON(needs) }}
          IS_MAIN: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name == 'push' }}
        run: bash scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${NEEDS_JSON:?NEEDS_JSON is required (pass toJSON(needs))}"
IS_MAIN="${IS_MAIN:-false}"

select_by_result() {
  printf '%s' "$NEEDS_JSON" \
    | jq -r --arg want "$1" \
        'to_entries | map(select(.value.result == $want) | .key) | join(", ")'
}

failed="$(select_by_result failure)"
cancelled="$(select_by_result cancelled)"

echo "Failed jobs:    ${failed:-<none>}"
echo "Cancelled jobs: ${cancelled:-<none>}"

status=0
if [ -n "$failed" ]; then
  echo "::error::Pipeline failed. Failing jobs: ${failed}"
  status=1
fi
if [ -n "$cancelled" ]; then
  if [ "$IS_MAIN" = "true" ]; then
    echo "::error::Pipeline has cancelled jobs on main: ${cancelled}. A job killed by 'timeout-minutes' is reported as cancelled, which would otherwise hide the failure."
    status=1
  else
    echo "::warning::Cancelled jobs: ${cancelled}. On a non-default ref this is usually a superseded run."
  fi
fi
exit "$status"
```

Two details worth keeping:

- **`needs:` must list every job.** Any job left out can still time out unobserved. A test that diffs the job list against the gate's `needs:` catches drift — that is exactly how I found a missing job in my own implementation.
- **Always print both lists before deciding.** The next grey run then explains itself in its own log instead of requiring a 25 000-line log download.

The implementation, a behavioural test over all four conclusion states, and the full incident reconstruction are in link-assistant/formal-ai#977 / [PR #978](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/978).

+  "body": "## Summary

`.jscpd.json` in this template sets `"format": "console"`. In jscpd, `format` is the list of **languages/formats to analyze**, not the output format — output is controlled by `reporters` (which this file already sets correctly).

Because `console` is not a source language, jscpd matches **zero files** and always reports `Found 0 clones.` The duplication gate is therefore a permanent false positive: it can never fail, no matter how much duplicated code a repository contains.

Found while working on [link-foundation/start#158](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/158) ("check for all false positives, false negatives, warnings and errors in CI/CD").

## Reproducible example

Two deliberately identical files plus this template's `format` setting:

```bash
mkdir jscpd-repro && cd jscpd-repro
printf 'function a(){\n  const x=1;\n  const y=2;\n  const z=3;\n  return x+y+z;\n}\n' > a.js
printf 'function b(){\n  const x=1;\n  const y=2;\n  const z=3;\n  return x+y+z;\n}\n' > b.js
printf '{"threshold":0,"minTokens":10,"minLines":3,"format":"console","reporters":["console"]}' > .jscpd.json

npx --yes jscpd .
```

Actual output:

```
Found 0 clones.
```

Exit code `0` — the gate passes despite 100 % duplication between the two files.

Remove `"format": "console"` (or set it to real languages) and re-run:

```bash
npx --yes jscpd . --format javascript
```

```
Found 1 clones.
ERROR: jscpd found too many duplicates (41.7%) over threshold (0.0%)
```

This is not theoretical for real repositories either: in a repository using this template's config verbatim, `npx jscpd .` reports "No duplicates found", while `npx jscpd . --format "javascript"` on the same tree reports 24 files / 49 clones / **5.64 %** duplication.

## Workaround

Override on the command line until the config is fixed:

```bash
npx jscpd . --format "javascript,typescript,jsx,tsx,markdown"
```

## Suggested fix

Drop the `format` key so jscpd uses its default language set, or list the languages the repository actually contains. `reporters` already carries the console output, so nothing is lost:

```diff
   "ignore": [
     ...
   ],
-  "format": "console",
   "reporters": ["console", "html"],
   "output": "./reports/jscpd"
 }
```

or, to be explicit:

```diff
-  "format": "console",
+  "format": ["javascript", "jsx", "typescript", "tsx", "json", "markdown", "yaml"],
```

Note that fixing this will make the gate start reporting real duplication, so repositories adopting the fix may need to set a non-zero `threshold` (or extend `ignore`) in the same change rather than being surprised by a suddenly red pipeline.

## Suggested regression test

Since the failure mode is silent, a check that jscpd actually analyzed something is worth adding to the workflow — e.g. assert the JSON reporter's `statistics.total.sources > 0`, so a future config typo fails loudly instead of turning the gate green.

+  "body": "## Summary

The current `scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh` enforces a hard 1500-line limit but has **no warn band**. Two PRs that each individually keep a file under 1500 can together push it over after both merge — the second PR's CI passes pre-merge, then the post-merge check on `main` is the first failure signal. Downstream Docker / Helm / Release jobs are then gated and skipped until someone notices.

This pattern has bitten downstream consumers of the template repeatedly:

- [`link-assistant/hive-mind` issue #1593](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1593) — original concurrent-merge race.
- [`link-assistant/hive-mind` issue #1730](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/1730) — same shape, single PR adding a small block to many files near the threshold; case study at <https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/case-studies/issue-1730/README.md>.

## Reproduction

1. In any repo using this template, prepare two PRs that each modify the same `.mjs` file.
2. Each PR alone leaves the file under 1500 lines (e.g. file is at 1499, PR-A adds 1 line, PR-B adds 1 line).
3. Merge PR-A. Merge PR-B. Both CI runs were green pre-merge.
4. The first CI run on `main` after PR-B fails: `ERROR: file has 1500 lines (limit: 1500)` (or above).
5. Release / build jobs are skipped because `check-file-line-limits` is a required gate.

## Suggested fix

Port the `WARN_THRESHOLD=1350` band from `link-assistant/hive-mind`'s version of the script. The 150-line gap (10% headroom) is enough to absorb typical concurrent-PR drift without being so tight that benign refactors are noisy.

Patch (functionally what hive-mind does today):

```bash
LIMIT=1500
WARN_THRESHOLD=1350
FAILURES=()
WARNINGS=()

# inside the find loop, after the >LIMIT check:
elif [ "\$line_count" -gt "\$WARN_THRESHOLD" ]; then
  WARNINGS+=(\"\$file\")
fi

# after the loop, before the failure summary:
if [ \"\${#WARNINGS[@]}\" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo \"\"
  echo \"The following files are approaching the \${LIMIT} line limit (>\${WARN_THRESHOLD} lines):\"
  printf '  %s\n' \"\${WARNINGS[@]}\"
  echo \"\"
  echo \"Consider extracting code to prevent concurrent PR merge limit violations.\"
fi
```

Hive-mind's version is here for reference: <https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh>.

Optionally, project owners can promote warnings to errors in PRs that touch warn-band files, but the warn-only behavior is sufficient on its own — it gives reviewers a visible cue to pause and refactor before the file becomes a concurrent-merge hazard.

## Out-of-scope follow-up

While auditing the template against the same downstream incident, I noticed:

- The template's `eslint.config.js` already uses the shorthand `'max-lines': ['error', 1500]` (defaults `skipBlankLines: false, skipComments: false`), so it does **not** have the ESLint-vs-CI desync bug we just fixed in hive-mind. No change needed there.

Just adding the warn band would close the remaining gap.",

+  "body": "The release workflow uses `actions/checkout@v6` but does not set Git's default initial branch before checkout runs. On GitHub-hosted runners with Git 2.54, checkout initializes the repository before any user-defined step can run and emits this warning:

```text
hint: Using 'master' as the name for the initial branch. This default branch name
hint: will change to "main" in Git 3.0. To configure the initial branch name
hint: to use in all of your new repositories, which will suppress this warning,
hint: call:
hint:
hint:  git config --global init.defaultBranch <name>
```

Observed example: https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-pull-all/actions/runs/28363495995

Related downstream fix: https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-pull-all/pull/47

## Reproduction

1. Run any workflow job in this template that starts with `actions/checkout@v6` on a runner where Git emits the Git 3.0 default-branch hint.
2. Inspect the checkout log. The warning appears during checkout's internal `git init`, before a normal workflow step could run `git config --global init.defaultBranch main`.

Local reproduction of the workaround:

```bash
git init /tmp/git-default-branch-warning

GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1 \
GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=init.defaultBranch \
GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0=main \
git init /tmp/git-default-branch-configured
```

The configured command initializes the repository without the default-branch hint.

## Workaround

Set Git runtime config at workflow scope so it is present for `actions/checkout` itself, not only for later shell steps:

```yaml
env:
  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
```

## Suggested Fix

Add the workflow-level env block above to `.github/workflows/release.yml` and add a workflow contract test that asserts it remains present. This keeps CI logs free of false-positive warnings and avoids relying on runner-global Git configuration.

+  "body": "## Summary

The npm resolver installs version-specific packages as global aliases such as
`zx-v-latest@npm:zx@8.8.5` and `zx-v-8.8.5@npm:zx@8.8.5`. If the package exposes
a binary, the second alias fails with `EEXIST` because both aliases claim the
original package's binary name (`zx`). This prevents a caller from migrating a
bare `use('zx')` import to reproducible `use('zx@8.8.5')` on an existing
installation.

Found while fixing link-assistant/hive-mind#2150. This is distinct from #72,
which concerns Node 24 CommonJS namespace unwrapping.

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
prefix="$(mktemp -d)"
npm install -g --prefix "$prefix" zx-v-latest@npm:zx@8.8.5
npm install -g --prefix "$prefix" zx-v-8.8.5@npm:zx@8.8.5
```

Observed with npm 11.17.0:

```text
npm error code EEXIST
npm error path <prefix>/bin/zx
npm error EEXIST: file already exists
npm error File exists: <prefix>/bin/zx
```

The repository reproducer is
`experiments/issue-2150/reproduce-use-m-bin-alias-conflict.sh` in Hive Mind PR
#2151. It uses a temporary prefix and verifies the error and binary path.

## Expected

Multiple use-m aliases for the same package can coexist, including packages
with `bin` entries. Loading a version-pinned module should not require deleting
the former `-v-latest` alias or an unrelated global executable.

## Root cause

`use-m` runs:

```text
npm install -g <alias>@npm:<package>@<version>
```

npm gives a global alias the package's original `bin` names. Alias directory
names are unique, but their global executable paths are not.

## Workaround

Hive Mind PR #2151 first verifies that the conflicting executable symlink
targets another use-m alias for the same package, then retries npm with
`--force --no-bin-links`. The versioned module alias installs, both aliases
remain, and npm 11 leaves the original executable symlink unchanged. Clean CI
preinstallation also uses `--no-bin-links`.

Never use `--force` without verifying ownership: the path may belong to a
user-installed global package rather than use-m.

## Suggested fix

The npm resolver should treat package binaries as unnecessary because use-m
imports modules; it does not invoke their global CLIs. On `EEXIST`, it can:

1. parse the conflicting executable path;
2. resolve its symlink target;
3. verify the target is `<globalRoot>/<same-package>-v-*/...`;
4. retry the alias install without bin links (using `--force` only after that
   ownership check, because npm 11 still performs the collision check with
   `--no-bin-links` alone).

A regression test should install `zx-v-latest`, then resolve `zx@8.8.5` in the
same isolated prefix and assert that both module aliases remain loadable.

+{
+  "body": "## Summary

`use-m@8.15.0` returns the wrong module shape on Node.js 24 when its npm resolver imports a CommonJS package whose `module.exports` is a callable object. The returned object has only `default` and `module.exports`; named properties attached to the callable default are not exposed at the top level.

This broke every `use('command-stream')` consumer in `link-assistant/hive-mind` after `command-stream@0.19.0` added its CommonJS entry point: callers expect `(await use('command-stream')).$`, but Node 24 gets `undefined`.

Downstream incident: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2150

## Minimal reproduction

```bash
npx --yes node@24 --input-type=module -e "
  const code = await (await fetch('https://unpkg.com/use-m@8.15.0/use.js')).text();
  const { use } = await eval(code);
  const loaded = await use('command-stream@0.19.0');
  console.log({
    node: process.version,
    type: typeof loaded,
    keys: Object.keys(loaded),
    dollar: typeof loaded?.\$,
    default: typeof loaded?.default,
    moduleExports: typeof loaded?.['module.exports'],
    defaultDollar: typeof loaded?.default?.\$,
  });
"
```

Actual Node 24 output:

```text
{
  node: 'v24.19.0',
  type: 'object',
  keys: [ 'default', 'module.exports' ],
  dollar: 'undefined',
  default: 'function',
  moduleExports: 'function',
  defaultDollar: 'function'
}
```

The same command with `node@20` returns the callable default directly and `dollar` is `function`.

## Root cause

Node 23.0.0+ adds a synthetic `'module.exports'` named export to CommonJS namespaces. In `src/use.js`, `baseUse()` unwraps `module.default` only when every other key is included in `metadataKeys`. That set includes `default` and `__esModule`, but not the new `module.exports` interop marker. It therefore treats the marker as a meaningful named export and returns the two-key namespace instead of the callable default.

`use-m` reaches the CommonJS entry because its npm path resolver uses `createRequire(...).resolve`, so the `require` export condition is selected even though the resolved file is subsequently loaded with dynamic `import()`.

Node documents the synthetic marker here: https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#commonjs-namespaces

## Workarounds

Consumers can normalize either shape:

```js
const loaded = await use('command-stream@0.19.0');
const commandStream = loaded?.default ?? loaded;
const $ = loaded?.$ ?? commandStream?.$ ?? commandStream;
```

Packages can also keep an ESM-only `main`/`exports` path, but that removes the CommonJS support that `command-stream@0.19.0` intentionally added.

## Suggested fix

At minimum, treat `'module.exports'` as CJS metadata in `baseUse()`:

+## Summary
+
+`use-m@8.15.0` returns the wrong module shape on Node.js 24 when its npm resolver imports a CommonJS package whose `module.exports` is a callable object. The returned object has only `default` and `module.exports`; named properties attached to the callable default are not exposed at the top level.
+
+This broke every `use('command-stream')` consumer in `link-assistant/hive-mind` after `command-stream@0.19.0` added its CommonJS entry point: callers expect `(await use('command-stream')).$`, but Node 24 gets `undefined`.
+
+Downstream incident: https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2150
+
+## Minimal reproduction
+
+```bash
+npx --yes node@24 --input-type=module -e "
+  const code = await (await fetch('https://unpkg.com/use-m@8.15.0/use.js')).text();
+  const { use } = await eval(code);
+  const loaded = await use('command-stream@0.19.0');
+  console.log({
+    node: process.version,
+    type: typeof loaded,
+    keys: Object.keys(loaded),
+    dollar: typeof loaded?.\$,
+    default: typeof loaded?.default,
+    moduleExports: typeof loaded?.['module.exports'],
+    defaultDollar: typeof loaded?.default?.\$,
+  });
+"
+```
+
+Actual Node 24 output:
+
+```text
+{
+  node: 'v24.19.0',
+  type: 'object',
+  keys: [ 'default', 'module.exports' ],
+  dollar: 'undefined',
+  default: 'function',
+  moduleExports: 'function',
+  defaultDollar: 'function'
+}
+```
+
+The same command with `node@20` returns the callable default directly and `dollar` is `function`.
+
+## Root cause
+
+Node 23.0.0+ adds a synthetic `'module.exports'` named export to CommonJS namespaces. In `src/use.js`, `baseUse()` unwraps `module.default` only when every other key is included in `metadataKeys`. That set includes `default` and `__esModule`, but not the new `module.exports` interop marker. It therefore treats the marker as a meaningful named export and returns the two-key namespace instead of the callable default.
+
+`use-m` reaches the CommonJS entry because its npm path resolver uses `createRequire(...).resolve`, so the `require` export condition is selected even though the resolved file is subsequently loaded with dynamic `import()`.
+
+Node documents the synthetic marker here: https://nodejs.org/api/esm.html#commonjs-namespaces
+
+## Workarounds
+
+Consumers can normalize either shape:
+
+```js
+const loaded = await use('command-stream@0.19.0');
+const commandStream = loaded?.default ?? loaded;
+const $ = loaded?.$ ?? commandStream?.$ ?? commandStream;
+```
+
+Packages can also keep an ESM-only `main`/`exports` path, but that removes the CommonJS support that `command-stream@0.19.0` intentionally added.
+
+## Suggested fix
+
+At minimum, treat `'module.exports'` as CJS metadata in `baseUse()`:
+
+```diff
+ const metadataKeys = new Set([
+-  'default', '__esModule', 'Symbol(Symbol.toStringTag)',
++  'default', 'module.exports', '__esModule', 'Symbol(Symbol.toStringTag)',
+```
+
+More robustly, when `module.default === module['module.exports']`, regard both keys as the same CommonJS default and unwrap it. Please add a Node 24 regression fixture whose CommonJS export is a function with enumerable properties, and assert `use()` preserves the callable shape and its attached properties.
+
+## Evidence
+
+The failing Hive Mind run was on Node 24 and failed in three independent jobs with `TypeError: $ is not a function`. The standalone reproduction above produces the exact missing `$` shape; Node 20 is a passing control.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Reproduce use-m's npm alias collision without touching the real global prefix.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+test_prefix="$(mktemp -d)"
+cleanup() {
+  case "$test_prefix" in
+    /tmp/*) rm -rf "$test_prefix" ;;
+    *) echo "Refusing to remove unexpected path: $test_prefix" >&2 ;;
+  esac
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+echo "Isolated npm prefix: $test_prefix"
+npm install -g --prefix "$test_prefix" zx-v-latest@npm:zx@8.8.5
+
+set +e
+npm install -g --prefix "$test_prefix" zx-v-8.8.5@npm:zx@8.8.5 > "$test_prefix/conflict.log" 2>&1
+status=$?
+set -e
+
+cat "$test_prefix/conflict.log"
+if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "Expected the second alias to fail with EEXIST" >&2
+  exit 1
+fi
+grep -q 'EEXIST' "$test_prefix/conflict.log"
+grep -q '/bin/zx' "$test_prefix/conflict.log"
+echo "Reproduced: second use-m alias cannot share the package binary (exit $status)."

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Turn timeout cancellations into visible failures on the release branch.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+: "${NEEDS_JSON:?NEEDS_JSON is required (pass toJSON(needs))}"
+IS_MAIN="${IS_MAIN:-false}"
+
+select_by_result() {
+  NEEDS_JSON="$NEEDS_JSON" WANT_RESULT="$1" node --input-type=module -e '
+    const needs = JSON.parse(process.env.NEEDS_JSON);
+    const jobs = Object.entries(needs)
+      .filter(([, value]) => value.result === process.env.WANT_RESULT)
+      .map(([name]) => name);
+    console.log(jobs.join(", "));
+  '
+}
+
+failed="$(select_by_result failure)"
+cancelled="$(select_by_result cancelled)"
+
+echo "Failed jobs:    ${failed:-<none>}"
+echo "Cancelled jobs: ${cancelled:-<none>}"
+
+status=0
+
+if [ -n "$failed" ]; then
+  echo "::error::Pipeline failed. Failing jobs: ${failed}"
+  status=1
+fi
+
+if [ -n "$cancelled" ]; then
+  if [ "$IS_MAIN" = "true" ]; then
+    echo "::error::Pipeline has cancelled jobs on main: ${cancelled}. A job killed by 'timeout-minutes' is reported as cancelled, which would otherwise hide the failure."
+    status=1
+  else
+    echo "::warning::Cancelled jobs: ${cancelled}. On a non-default ref this is usually a superseded run."
+  fi
+fi
+
+if [ "$status" -eq 0 ]; then
+  echo "All required jobs succeeded or were legitimately skipped."
+fi
+
+exit "$status"
